problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Column Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The matrix $M$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(M).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{m}_{1}+{x}_{2}{m}_{2}+{x}_{3}{m}_{3},$ and ${m}_{1}$, ${m}_{2}$, and ${m}_{3}$ are the respective columns of $M.$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 6 & 0 & -13\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 16\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(M),$ we need to check if the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[M\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[M\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 6 & 0 & -13 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 6 & 0 & -13 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=2 \\ -3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=10 \\ {x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting it into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2}+2(-1) & =10 \\ -3{x}_{2}-2 & =10 \\ -3{x}_{2} & =12 \\ {x}_{2} & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+(-4)-5(-1) & =2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+1 & =2 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =1 \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(M).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${m}_{1},$ ${m}_{2},$ and ${m}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 16\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{1}}+(-4)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{2}}+(-1)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -13\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-4)\cdot (-1)=2.$
